title: Lower Burgundy
capsule: Lower Burgundy (Regnum Provinciae) was a Carolingian successor kingdom carved out of the Rhône valley and Provence in 879 when Boso of Vienne, brother-in-law of Charles the Bald, was elected king by local magnates and bishops at Mantaille — the first non-Carolingian to be elevated to kingship in the Frankish world. The kingdom encompassed the lower Rhône corridor south to the Mediterranean, including Arles, Vienne, and Marseille. In 933 it was united with Upper Burgundy by Rudolf II of Transjurane Burgundy to form the Kingdom of Arles (Burgundy), ending Lower Burgundy's separate existence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The polity's territory is reconstructed from Carolingian diplomas and episcopal lists; precise frontiers, especially toward northern Burgundy and Italy, are disputed in the scholarship.
